texts.content:
The common converted human loses all conscious identity,
yet retains muscle memory, conditioned reflexes, and movement
patterns that the plague repurposes with surgical precision.
Its body rapidly adapts to close-quarters
combat: limbs are reinforced with external vascular tissue,
forming semi-organic structures
that enhance strength, durability, and grip.

This humanoid form is the most versatile
within the swarm, and therefore the most likely to
evolve into specialized units such as giants or soldiers.
The plague exploits the neuromuscular
architecture of the human body to construct tactical variants
capable of wielding serrated weapons, executing complex
maneuvers, and coordinating attacks. In many cases, converted
humans act as transitional nodes, catalyzing advanced
mutations or leading smaller swarms with brutal efficiency.
